guide.title: How coupons work
guide.subtitle: The discounts are Medusa promotions. This panel creates them, describes them in one sentence and adds rules Medusa does not have.

start.title: Create a coupon in three steps
start.text:
Kind: what the customer gets. Who for: everyone, chosen groups or chosen customers. Rules: a code or automatic, dates, limits, minimum basket and exclusions.
The panel on the right shows what the customer will see and warns you before you save.

kinds.title: Kinds of discount
kinds.text: Percentage or amount off the order, free shipping, a discount on chosen categories, buy X get Y, and tiers. Amounts are gross.

who.title: Who for
who.text:
Everyone means guests and signed-in customers. Groups and chosen customers need the customer to be signed in.
"First order only" checks earlier orders by customer account, and by e-mail for guests. Cancelled orders do not count.

rules.title: Limits
rules.text: The total limit counts all customers together. The limit per customer counts by customer account, and by e-mail for guests. The minimum basket is gross, before discounts, without shipping.

combining.title: Combining coupons
combining.text:
"Does not combine" means: no other code can be added next to it, and automatic coupons step aside while it is in the cart. An automatic coupon that does not combine steps aside as soon as the customer enters any code.
Promotions made in Medusa outside this panel are not changed: when one of them is already in the cart, a coupon that does not combine is refused.

tiers.title: Tiers
tiers.text: One coupon, several levels, e.g. 5% from 200 zł and 10% from 500 zł. The customer gets the highest level the basket reaches, never two at once. In Medusa promotions each level is a separate promotion with a code ending in __T1, __T2.

batches.title: Batches of single-use codes
batches.text:
A prefix and a number, e.g. 500 codes starting with NL-. Each code works once. The list shows which code was used and in which order; download it as CSV.
Other plugins (a newsletter, say) are told about a new batch through the bitshaft.coupons.batch_created event.

checks.title: Checked on the server
checks.text: Every rule is checked by the store's server when a code is added and again before the order is placed, never only in the browser. The customer sees why a code was refused, in Polish and English.

storefront.title: For the storefront
storefront.text: The storefront can check a code before adding it (POST /store/coupons/check) and show how much is missing to the next tier or free shipping (GET /store/coupons/progress). See the plugin README.

limits.title: Good to know
limits.text:
Editing keeps the usage counts. The code, the kind of discount and automatic or not cannot change; duplicate the coupon for that.
Deleting a coupon does not change orders that already used it.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Values for new coupons and exports. Only what you change is stored; the rest follows the plugin options.
settings.optionsHint: Set in medusa-config.ts. Change them there and restart Medusa.

options.checkRateLimitPerMinute: Code checks per visitor per minute

demo.body: "Restore test data" creates a set of demo coupons as real Medusa promotions: every kind, tiers, an automatic coupon, limits, a first-order coupon, a customer group, exclusions, every status and a batch of single-use codes. Their names start with [Demo] and their codes with DEMO-. Turn the demo option off in medusa-config.ts before going live.
demo.resetBody: Coupons named [Demo] are deleted with their promotions and created again. They are real promotions: their codes work at checkout while they are active. Your own coupons are not touched.
